bodyEdits.before: During the campaign against Wrath, Draygar approaches Death and is offered a bargain involving his hammer. The temptation is concrete because it touches the tool, calling, and strength through which he understands himself. He refuses to let the bargain decide his allegiance and later throws Wrath’s sword away, denying the enemy both possession and symbolic control.
bodyEdits.after: After Saray kills Wrath, Draygar picks up the fallen sword and throws it at Death, accusing him of bringing only death despite his talk of a beautiful world. Later, when Death refuses to give the company weapons it could use against him, Draygar proposes a trade. He holds up Cala’s radiant warhammer and asks for Olokun’s return. Saray offers her own possessions; Krone holds out his maul and asks for his new family back. Death rejects objects in exchange for souls and closes the door. Draygar answers, “Well.... Ay tried.” The exchange ends without an accepted bargain or the hammer changing hands.

bodyEdits.before: Draygar’s failure mode is not simple rage. It is the belief that because he can bear a burden, he should accept it before asking whether another plan exists. His strongest scenes resist that trap by making strength collaborative: rescue someone, carry information, consult Gartina, and refuse an enemy’s attempt to define service as surrender.
bodyEdits.after: Draygar’s willingness to go first can leave him hurt and relying on companions. At the Citadel he accepts Wren’s potions and waits while others make the passage safe. Anger and strength do not win his friends back from Death; he still has to decide what to do next. His work includes rescue, carrying information and consulting Gartina, alongside fights he cannot settle by hitting harder.
bodyEdits.reason: Replace an asserted private failure motive with specific witnessed reliance, restraint and unsuccessful action; retain rescue, communication and consultation.

fieldEdits.before: Across Pristinia, Gael, The Before, and the campaign against Wrath, Draygar repeatedly uses his strength to rescue others. He carries the warhammer Cala, rejects Death’s attempt to turn grief into a bargain, and throws Wrath’s sword away. He earns Captain Zythienne’s promised recommendation to Captain Tarwen after the dragon-isle battle; this exchange alone does not establish formal Silver Star admission.
